summary: [¶] (ix) The present Petition was filed in August 2023, and it is clear that the issues, facts, and documents sought to be produced by way of the amendment relate to the period much prior to the filing of the Petition. There is no dispute that the issues and aspects sought to be raised were known and available with the Petitioner, prior to the filing of the Petition and in any case, before the final hearing in the Commission. The proposed amendment constitutionally or fundamentally changes the nature and character of the case. The Petition was filed for Change in Law in regard to Government of Gujarat Resolutions, 2021, and now the Petitioner is seeking to introduce not only new Change in Law events but also force majeure events; [¶] the same cannot be a reason to seek amendment of the Petition at the belated stage. The objection was taken on the delays in commissioning and the fact that the Change in Law claims of the Petitioner arise after the SCOD. It was the Petitioner’s stand that Change in Law claims are independent of the force majeure claims and sought to rely on the Order dated 5.3.2024 in Appeal No. 52 of 2024. GUVNL had made submissions on the claim of Change in Law and had also opposed the contention of the Petitioner that there cannot be any consideration of Change in Law, and the Petition is only for the verification. The Petitioner was, therefore, well aware of the objections of GUVNL and other Respondents, but admittedly chose not to seek any amendment at that stage and the Petitioner has to suffer the consequences thereof. [¶] (xi) In fact, Petition No. 131/MP/2024 and the present Petition were also heard together in part, where this specific issue of scope of Change in Law Rules 2021 was argued vide Record of Proceeding for the hearing on 29.4.2024 and 8.5.2024 and thereafter listed on 5.9.2024 and 30.9.2024, though thereafter the arguments were addressed separately. Merely because Petition No. 131/MP/2023 was decided first, does not mean that the Petitioner can now seek to change its stand or improve its case. This is not a subsequent development necessitating any addressal of even oral arguments, let alone any amendment. [¶] (i) The Petitioner filed the Application to amend the Original Petition to include its Force Majeure events and pre-CIL Rules Change in Law claims under the present proceedings – specifically to avoid multiplicity of proceedings and piecemeal adjudication of the Petitioner’s claims. Thus, the amendment Application filed by the Petitioner should be allowed since the present Application is, in fact, in compliance with the MUML Order issued by the Commission. [¶] (xi) There is no delay on the part of the Petitioner, and the IA is not barred by limitation. The present Application merely seeks to align the Petition with the prevailing legal position as per the Order in the MUML matter. Further, no prejudice will be caused to the Respondents if the present Application is allowed, as no new factual evidence qua the claims raised in the Original Petition is introduced and the amendment only ensures that ‘adjudication’ is conclusive with respect to the Petitioner’s Force Majeure and Change in Law claims under the TSA. [¶] amendment of the Pleadings even after the conclusion of the final hearing and the reservation of the Order in the Petition.
